did_you_know.text: Did you know? The book of Proverbs opens by presenting the words of Solomon son of David, king of Israel, as the source of the proverbs in the book.
Did you know? The purpose of the book is to impart wisdom and discipline, and to help the reader understand insightful sayings.
Did you know? Even a wise person never stops learning: the verse says that the wise will increase in learning, and the discerning will gain guidance and practical understanding.
Did you know? The book of Proverbs deals not only with proverbs, but also with sayings, the words of the wise, and riddles—different kinds of statements that require understanding and interpretation.
Did you know? According to the chapter, the fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge; in contrast, fools despise wisdom and discipline.
Did you know? The instruction in this chapter includes both a father's discipline and a mother's teaching, so both parents are presented as important sources of guidance.
Did you know? The warning against sin is given at the very beginning of the temptation: even if others try to persuade him, the son must not agree to join them.
Did you know? The chapter teaches that pursuing ill-gotten gain can ultimately harm the person seeking profit as well, since greed 'takes the life of its owner.'
Did you know? Wisdom is portrayed as a figure calling aloud in the streets and raising her voice in public places—showing that the message of wisdom is available to everyone.
Did you know? The chapter ends with a clear contrast: whoever listens to wisdom will live in safety and peace, while rejecting wisdom is described as bringing disaster and fear.
